title: His children
summary: He talks about his children from Flo and their distance from him.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Where are you children?
One son is in a hospital, my oldest son. My next son is in Las Vegas-- oh, he's back in Pennsylvania.
In the Poconos.
One of the hotels?
Yeah. I think it's Host Farm.
And my daughter, I heard, got married recently in California.
Last year.
I didn't hear about it until about a month ago.
These are children of Flo?
Right. Flo's children. My oldest son is trying to out do me in that period. He wants to be sicker than
his father was.
I also didn't mean-- the kids, obviously have grown away and such--
Right.
Do the kids have any idea who dad was, or is?--strike 'was'.
I don't know. I would think they do. They know what I've done, they know that I write music and I play. What they know beyond that I don't know, because I haven't seen them.
I don't think this is so much a question about George Handy's children, but sort of everybody's kids. We're talking about the people who are important to jazz--
(Volume of tape became extremely low at this point and parts were inaudible to transcriber.)
I'm sure my kids wouldn't have the foggiest idea of what I was doing in 1945 and yours--
I really don't know.
I'm sure this segment isn't going anywhere. It seemed like a good idea. You said that David ran into your daughter and she began questioning him.
Right, which surprised me, because if she was interested, why doesn't she phone me and ask me the questions.
The answer to that is very obvious, from an old father like me.
Tell me.

It's not that easy to do the obvious and clear thing. I'm sure you're the world's greatest expert. That's why you can't do the obvious thing to family, and parents; tell me about your mother again. I'm sure your mother would say why doesn't he call me when we have such a problem. Does that sound preachy?
I hear what you're saying, Bill.
I'm the world's greatest expert, I've got the world's greatest void with kids too.
